modern: Epictetus also said that a man must find an art, or rules, for giving his assent; and as to his impulses, he must take care that they are made with regard to circumstances, that they are consistent with the common good, and that they have regard to the value of the object; and as for sensual desire, he should keep away from it altogether; and as for aversion, he should not show it towards any of the things which are not in our power.
original: Epictetus also said, a man must discover an art [or rules] with respect to giving his assent; and in respect to his movements he must be careful that they be made with regard to circumstances, that they be consistent with social interests, that they have regard to the value of the object; and as to sensual desire, he should altogether keep away from it; and as to avoidance [aversion], he should not show it with respect to any of the things which are not in our power.

explained.summary: More from Epictetus, on three areas of inner discipline. First, learn a method for deciding what to accept as true, rather than agreeing to every impression. Second, make sure your impulses to act take account of circumstances, serve the common good and match what the thing is really worth. Third, keep away from craving altogether, and don’t feel aversion towards anything outside your control.
explained.today: Before believing the alarming headline, check it. Before jumping into a new project, ask whether it fits the moment and helps anyone. And when the flight is delayed, notice that resenting it changes nothing, since the delay was never yours to control.
